title: How to program your training yourself
summary: Part 2 of a three-part series on writing your own program. NH explains how to build the exercise list (only lifts done regularly for 3+ months that agree with you) and why full body or PPL are the best first templates. He covers matching the novice program's tonnage, keeping it minimalist, refining the draft while still running the novice program, and how long the process takes; his own final program took about four years.
claims: Write your program while still running your novice program; a year can pass between drafting it and starting it
The exercise list is the backbone of the program; without it you cannot program well
Only include lifts you have done regularly for at least three months and that agree with you: no painful lifts and no YouTube novelties
If the exercise selection is rotten, the whole program stinks
For a first self-made program he advises against bro splits (terrible format), gentleman splits and upper/lower (more advanced); full body or PPL work best

Full body and PPL are restrictive yet open, which helps beginners fit the pieces; programming is a puzzle where exercises are the pieces, volume, intensity and frequency the arrangement, and the template the frame
People with the best natural physiques program for themselves; jumping between internet programs will not get you there
You are the person best suited to program for yourself because of your empirical self-knowledge, once your knowledge catches up with a coach's
Model the new program on the novice program you are running and match its tonnage, so volume and intensity do not jump
Many people crash going from novice to intermediate because their new program adds far too much volume
Copy your novice rep ranges, and stay minimalist with a healthy dose of reductionism; avoid a laundry list of exercises
A first draft will look terrible; refine it occasionally while still running the novice program, without obsessing or getting greedy
You stop being a novice when you want to jump on your own program and explore
Switching to your own program will not cost gains because it mimics the novice program; even if it did, the programming skill is worth more over a 10-year career
Alpha and beta testing in the gym refine the program toward a final program, which for bodybuilders is the holy grail
His final program took close to four years: two years running a program to gather information, six months writing, two years of beta testing, finalized about four months ago
Muscles stop growing when your brain's ability to push them stops evolving; you have to learn programming
